title: Massage Task & Session Update Standard
summary: Every massage session must be visible, trackable, and properly communicated from assignment to completion through the approved Task & Update Channel.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: At Zura Spa, every massage session must be visible, trackable, and properly communicated from assignment to completion through the approved Task & Update Channel, such as the designated WhatsApp group.

The purpose of the channel is to ensure that the entire relevant team knows who has been assigned, whether the therapists are preparing, when the client arrives, when the client proceeds to the room, whether required routines have been completed, when the massage starts, the current stage of the massage, any client request or concern, when the massage ends, when the client is preparing to leave, and anything the front desk or leadership needs to act on.
At Zura Spa, important session information should not exist only in one person's head, inside the massage room, or in a private conversation when the wider operational team needs to know it.
If the information affects the session, client, therapist, leadership, front desk, or next action, update the team.

sections.title: 1. Why the Massage Task & Update Standard Matters
paragraphs: The Task & Update Standard supports clear therapist assignment, preparation before client arrival, team visibility, better client experience, real-time session coordination, better client support, and accountability.

sections.title: Clear Therapist Assignment
paragraphs: Before a session begins, therapists should know that they have been assigned.
The update channel provides clear notice so that there is no "I didn't know," "Nobody told me," "I thought someone else was taking the client," or last-minute searching for therapists.

sections.title: Preparation Before Client Arrival
paragraphs: Assignment is not merely information. It is a prompt to prepare for the session.

Once assigned, therapists should begin ensuring personal readiness, Freshen-Up Routine is completed where required, uniform and appearance meet standard, massage room is ready, bed and supplies are ready, required equipment is available, and any client-specific information has been understood.

sections.title: Team Visibility
paragraphs: The same channel lets the team know that therapists are set and ready.
This means leadership and the Client Manager do not have to physically search for therapists to determine whether preparation has been completed.

sections.title: Better Client Experience
paragraphs: When the client's arrival is communicated immediately, assigned therapists can be ready before the client enters the room.

The client should not experience internal confusion such as therapists still getting ready, a room not being prepared, people asking who is assigned, or therapists being called repeatedly after the client is already waiting.

sections.title: Real-Time Session Coordination
paragraphs: Massage sessions have important milestones. Updating them allows leadership and other relevant staff to know exactly where the session is without interrupting the massage unnecessarily.

sections.title: Better Client Support
paragraphs: A client may need water, an adjustment, assistance, clarification, something from the front desk, a payment-related response, or support after the massage.
If the update is communicated immediately, the appropriate person can act.

sections.title: Accountability
paragraphs: The update trail shows who was assigned, when preparation happened, when the massage started, whether required routines were confirmed, when major milestones happened, when the massage ended, and any important request or incident.
This improves accountability without requiring constant physical supervision.

sections.title: 2. The Mindset
paragraphs: The therapist's mindset should be: "The team should not have to guess what is happening with my session."

Updating is part of the massage responsibility. A massage is not properly managed simply because the therapist is inside the room performing the service. The operational side of the session must also remain visible.
Update before someone needs to ask. A professional therapist should not have to be repeatedly chased for routine milestone updates.
Keep updates useful. The channel is not for unnecessary conversation. Updates should be short, clear, accurate, timely, and relevant.
Communicate problems early. If something is wrong, do not wait until the end of the massage to reveal it.

The update helps other people do their jobs. A message may prompt CM action, leader confirmation, front-desk action, client support, therapist support, or session follow-up. Your update is therefore not only for yourself.

sections.title: 3. The Massage Task & Update Procedure
paragraphs: Follow this procedure from assignment through session completion.

sections.title: Step 1 — Therapists Are Assigned
paragraphs: Once a booking or session is ready to be allocated, the assigned therapists are communicated through the approved task/update channel.
Example: Client Sam — 4 Hands Massage. Assigned: Thr. Jane & Thr. Clara. Please prepare for session.
The assigned therapists should acknowledge or begin preparation according to the approved process.

sections.title: Step 2 — Therapists Prepare
paragraphs: After assignment, therapists should immediately begin the relevant preparation routines.
This includes personal readiness, Appearance Standard, Freshen-Up Routine where required, room readiness, massage supplies, equipment, client information, and co-therapist coordination.

sections.title: Step 3 — Team Is Updated That Therapists Are Set
paragraphs: Once preparation is complete, the assigned therapists should ensure the team knows they are ready through the same channel.
Example: Thr. Jane & Thr. Clara set for Client Sam.
This means therapists ready, room ready, session can proceed when client is ready.
Do not indicate that you are set when you are still preparing.

sections.title: Step 4 — Client Arrival Is Communicated
paragraphs: When the client arrives, the relevant team should be promptly informed.
Example: Client Sam has arrived.
This alerts assigned therapists, CM, front desk, and relevant leaders. The therapists should move into active readiness.

sections.title: Step 5 — Client Proceeding to the Room Is Communicated
paragraphs: When the client is being processed and taken to the massage room: Client Sam proceeding to Room 2.

This tells assigned therapists that the session is about to begin. They should not still be eating, changing clothes, looking for massage oil, searching for towels, or fixing their appearance. They should already be ready.

sections.title: Step 6 — Pre-Massage / Freshen-Up Status Is Updated
paragraphs: Where the required Freshen-Up Routine has been completed, it should be updated and confirmed by the CM where required.
Example: Freshen-Up Routine done — awaiting CM confirmation. Then: Freshen-Up Routine confirmed by CM.
Confirmation should mean the routine has actually been completed to standard.

sections.title: Step 7 — Massage Start Is Updated
paragraphs: Once the massage actually begins: Massage Start — Client Sam — 3:14 PM.
The update should reflect the actual start, not when the client entered the room. This becomes an important session milestone.

sections.title: 4. Required Massage Progress Milestones
paragraphs: The following milestones should be communicated through the Task & Update Channel as they occur.

sections.title: 1. Massage Start
paragraphs: Example: Massage Start — Client Sam — 3:14 PM.

sections.title: 2. Freshen-Up Routine Done and Confirmed
paragraphs: Example: Freshen-Up Routine done and confirmed by CM.
Where confirmation is required, the routine should not merely be assumed.

sections.title: 3. Massage Mid Routine Done
paragraphs: When the Massage Mid Routine has been completed: Massage Mid Routine done — Client Sam.
This shows that the massage has progressed to the required point.

sections.title: 4. Mid Freshen-Up Routine Done and Confirmed
paragraphs: Where the Mid Freshen-Up Routine applies: Mid Freshen-Up Routine done — awaiting confirmation.
The appropriate leader role should then confirm. Example: Mid Freshen-Up Routine confirmed by LT.
The leader confirming may vary according to the operational structure.

sections.title: 5. Lunez Massage Start Now
paragraphs: When the Lunez Massage stage begins: Lunez Massage starting now — Client Sam.
This gives leadership visibility into the progress of the session.

sections.title: 6. Client Requests
paragraphs: Important client requests should be communicated immediately.
Example: Client Sam needs water.
The therapist should not unnecessarily leave the massage room if someone else can support the request. The update enables the appropriate team member to respond.

sections.title: 7. Client Questions
paragraphs: If the client asks something that requires another person or department:
Example: Client Sam has a question concerning membership. CM please assist after session.
Or: Client Sam is asking about an additional service. Please advise.
Do not guess when the question is outside your responsibility.

sections.title: 8. Client Concerns
paragraphs: Relevant concerns should be updated immediately.
Example: Client Sam reports discomfort around the left shoulder. Pressure adjusted.
Where escalation is necessary: SP, Client Sam has raised a concern about ____. Please assist.
The Task & Update Standard works together with the Escalation Standard.

sections.title: 9. Session Blockers
paragraphs: If something prevents the massage from progressing normally: Massage temporarily paused — issue with ____. SP please assist.
Do not allow the team to assume everything is progressing normally when it is not.

sections.title: 10. Massage End
paragraphs: When the actual massage ends: Massage End — Client Sam — 5:42 PM.
This is different from the client leaving the room.

sections.title: 11. Client Done and Will Be Down Soon
paragraphs: When the client is dressing or preparing to leave the treatment room: Client Sam done — will be down shortly.
This allows the front desk and CM to prepare for the Client Departure Routine.

sections.title: 12. Client Would Like to Tip
paragraphs: If the client expresses an intention to tip: Client Sam would like to tip — please remind at front desk during departure.
This allows the front desk to support the client's stated intention without the therapist having to pursue the client personally.
The update is for operational follow-through, not for pressuring the client.

sections.title: 5. Massage Session Update Flow
paragraphs: The typical session should be visible approximately as:

ASSIGNED → THERAPISTS PREPARING → THERAPISTS SET → CLIENT ARRIVED → CLIENT PROCEEDING TO ROOM → FRESHEN-UP ROUTINE DONE & CONFIRMED BY CM → MASSAGE START → MASSAGE MID ROUTINE DONE → MID FRESHEN-UP ROUTINE DONE & CONFIRMED BY LEADER → LUNEZ MASSAGE START → OTHER REQUESTS / CONCERNS / UPDATES AS REQUIRED → MASSAGE END → CLIENT DONE — WILL BE DOWN SOON → CLIENT DEPARTURE / FRONT-DESK FOLLOW-UP
This gives the team a clear operational picture of every active session.

sections.title: 6. Important Updates Beyond Milestones
paragraphs: Milestones are the minimum expected updates. Therapists should also communicate anything important that affects the session.

This includes client requests water, client requests a different pressure, client has a concern, client asks for something outside the therapist's authority, client wants to speak with the CM, client requests an additional service, client reports pain, client requests a particular therapist, therapist needs assistance, equipment develops a problem, a routine cannot be completed, massage is temporarily paused, client needs additional time, session is running significantly differently from expected, client indicates they would like to tip, anything relevant to Client Departure Routine, and anything requiring escalation.
If another person needs the information to act properly, communicate it.

sections.title: 7. Who Is Responsible for Updates?
paragraphs: The fact that two therapists are working together does not mean "I thought the other person updated."
For co-therapist sessions, therapists should understand who is responsible for posting updates.
Where leadership has assigned a lead therapist for the session, that therapist may carry the primary update responsibility.
However, both therapists remain responsible for ensuring that required updates are actually made.
If an important update has not been posted, do not ignore it because someone else was expected to do it.

sections.title: 8. Leader Confirmations
paragraphs: Some milestones require confirmation because the update is not merely informational.
Freshen-Up Routine: confirmed by CM where required.
Mid Freshen-Up Routine: confirmed by the relevant leader role, such as TG, LT, SP, CM, or SM according to the applicable process.
A leader should not confirm something they have not actually verified where verification is required.
Confirmation means: "This requirement has been checked and completed."

sections.title: 9. How Updates Should Be Written
paragraphs: Updates should be short enough to read quickly.
Good: Client Sam arrived. Thr. Jane & Thr. Clara set. Massage Start — 4:18 PM. Client Sam needs water. Mid Freshen-Up done — LT please confirm.
Poor: "So the client came some minutes ago and we are already inside and we wanted to say that we're about to start everything now."
The channel should remain operational and easy to scan.
The standard is: CLIENT → STATUS/ACTION → TIME OR REQUEST WHERE RELEVANT.

sections.title: 10. Accuracy of Updates
paragraphs: An update must represent what has actually happened.
Do not post "Massage Start" when the massage has not started.
Do not post "Freshen-Up done" when it has not been completed.
Do not post "Therapists set" while you are still preparing.
The update channel is an operational record. False updates destroy its usefulness.

sections.title: 11. Timeliness of Updates
paragraphs: An update that comes too late may be almost as ineffective as no update.
For example: If the client asks for water and the therapist reports it after the massage, the update no longer serves its purpose.
Updates should be made at or immediately around the relevant milestone — not thirty minutes later, at the end of the session, or only after being asked.
UPDATE AS IT HAPPENS.

sections.title: 12. Massage Task Update vs Gossip
paragraphs: The update channel is for operational information. It should not become a place for jokes, mocking clients, unnecessary commentary, complaints about therapists, emotional arguments, personal conversations, or irrelevant client information.
Good: Client Sam requested lower pressure. Adjusted.
Not appropriate: This client complains too much.
Good: Client Sam requested to speak with CM after session.
Not appropriate: This man has started again.
We communicate facts required to manage the service, not judgments about clients.

sections.title: 13. What Good Task & Session Updates Look Like
paragraphs: A properly managed session means the team does not need to ask: Who is taking this client? Are the therapists ready? Has the client entered? Has the massage started? Has Mid Routine happened? Has the Freshen-Up Routine been confirmed? Is the session still going? Has the massage ended? Is the client coming downstairs?
The answers should already be visible through the normal updates.

sections.title: 14. What the Opposite Looks Like
paragraphs: The opposite of this standard is a session where information exists only inside the massage room.

sections.title: Therapists Do Not Acknowledge Assignment
paragraphs: A therapist sees their name assigned but makes no effort to prepare. The client arrives and the team discovers the therapist is not ready.

sections.title: No "Set" Update
paragraphs: Nobody knows whether the room or therapist is ready. The CM must start searching physically for information.

sections.title: Client Arrival Is Not Communicated
paragraphs: The client is waiting while assigned therapists believe they have more time.

sections.title: Massage Starts Without Update
paragraphs: Leadership cannot accurately determine session timing or progress.

sections.title: Milestones Are Skipped
paragraphs: Nobody knows whether Freshen-Up Routine happened, Mid Routine happened, Mid Freshen-Up happened, or Lunez Massage started.

sections.title: Client Requests Stay Inside the Room
paragraphs: The therapist knows the client needs water but never communicates. The client waits unnecessarily.

sections.title: Important Concerns Are Reported Afterwards
paragraphs: At the end of the massage: "By the way, the client was complaining about something for the last hour."
That removes the team's opportunity to help while the problem is still active.

sections.title: Massage Ends Without Informing Front Desk
paragraphs: The client suddenly appears downstairs while nobody is prepared for departure or follow-up.

sections.title: Client Says They Want to Tip, But Nobody Updates
paragraphs: The client later leaves and the opportunity to simply remind them of something they themselves requested is missed.

sections.title: 15. Why Zura Spa Will Not Tolerate Poor Session Updates
paragraphs: Failure to update is not merely a WhatsApp issue. It affects operations.

When therapists repeatedly fail to update: clients wait unnecessarily, leaders have to chase information, front desk cannot prepare, other therapists cannot coordinate, milestones cannot be verified, requests are missed, complaints are discovered late, accountability becomes difficult, session timing becomes unreliable, and the team works reactively instead of proactively.
Updating the task channel is part of performing the massage responsibility, not an optional administrative extra.

sections.title: 16. Impact on the Team
paragraphs: Poor session updates force people to chase information, break coordination, create false emergencies, create unfair workload, weaken accountability, frustrate leadership, and affect front desk.

Instead of focusing on their own responsibilities, leaders and team members must repeatedly ask whether the massage has started, whether therapists are set, whether the client is still upstairs, or whether they have finished.
When one person's update is missing, several other people may not know what to do next.
Something that should have been communicated calmly 20 minutes earlier becomes urgent because nobody was informed.
Responsible therapists who update properly may be repeatedly asked to cover for therapists who are not prepared or cannot be located.
If there is no reliable update trail, it becomes difficult to understand what happened, when it happened, whether the required routine was completed, and who knew about the issue.
Leadership should be supervising service quality, not continually searching for basic session status.
The front desk cannot properly prepare for client departure, questions, tips, payments, additional bookings, or complaints if important information remains inside the massage room.

sections.title: 17. Impact on the Client
paragraphs: The client may never see the WhatsApp group. But they feel the result of good or bad updates.
Good updates create faster response, better preparation, smooth handovers, timely water or assistance, better departure, fewer interruptions, and a more organized experience.
Poor updates create waiting, confusion, delays, forgotten requests, poor follow-up, and staff appearing unprepared.
The internal communication system exists ultimately to improve the external client experience.

sections.title: 18. What Therapists Should Do
list: Monitor the approved Task & Update Channel.
Notice when they are assigned.
Prepare immediately after assignment.
Ensure their readiness is communicated.
Monitor client-arrival updates.
Be ready when the client is proceeding to the room.
Post required massage milestones.
Ensure required confirmations are obtained.
Update client requests immediately.
Update concerns promptly.
Ask questions through the appropriate channel.
Escalate issues when necessary.
Communicate blockers.
Update Massage End.
Inform the team when the client will be coming down.
Communicate relevant departure information.
Follow through on updates that require action.
Ensure co-therapist sessions remain properly updated.

sections.title: 19. What Therapists Should Not Do
list: Ignore task assignments.
Claim they did not know when the assignment was communicated through the approved channel.
Wait for repeated reminders before preparing.
Say they are set when they are not.
Allow the client to arrive before beginning basic preparation.
Start the massage without updating.
Skip required milestones.
Post false milestones.
Backdate updates simply to make the record look complete.
Wait until the end of the massage to post several missed milestones.
Ignore client requests that require team support.
Leave a client waiting for water without communicating.
Hide concerns until the massage ends.
Keep blockers to themselves.
Assume the co-therapist made the update without checking.
Expect leadership to repeatedly ask for progress.
Use the update group for gossip.
Make disrespectful comments about clients.
Post unnecessary private client information.
Turn an operational update into an argument.
Leave the client-departure team unaware that the client is coming down.
Treat updates as optional because the massage itself is going well.

sections.title: 20. Correction and Accountability
paragraphs: At Zura Spa: Missing an update once + correcting immediately = learning. Unclear update + improving it = development. Being prompted initially + becoming consistently proactive = growth.

But: Repeatedly failing to update = performance concern. Repeated false completion updates = serious accountability concern. Deliberately hiding a session issue = serious conduct concern. Repeatedly requiring leaders to chase basic milestone updates = failure to maintain the operational standard.
The objective is not to create unnecessary messaging. The objective is to ensure that every important session event is visible when the team needs to know it.

sections.title: 21. The Zura Spa Massage Task & Update Standard
paragraphs: ASSIGN → PREPARE → SET → ARRIVE → ROOM → CONFIRM → START → UPDATE → SUPPORT → END → DEPART

Every therapist should ask: Have I seen my assignment? Am I ready? Does the team know I am ready? Has client arrival been acknowledged? Has Massage Start been updated? Have required routines and confirmations been communicated? Does the team know the current massage milestone? Is there any request, question, blocker or concern the team needs to know? Has Massage End been updated? Does the front desk know the client is coming down? Is there anything they need to know for Client Departure?
DON'T LEAVE THE TEAM GUESSING.
DON'T WAIT TO BE CHASED.
DON'T KEEP IMPORTANT INFORMATION INSIDE THE ROOM.
DON'T REPORT A PROBLEM AFTER THE TIME TO SOLVE IT HAS PASSED.
UPDATE AS THE SESSION MOVES.
A well-performed massage requires skilled therapists. A well-managed massage requires the entire team to know what is happening and what needs to happen next.
KNOW THE TASK. PREPARE. UPDATE THE MILESTONE. COMMUNICATE THE NEED. COMPLETE THE SESSION. PROTECT THE EXPERIENCE.

remember: Update as the session moves. If another person needs the information to act properly, communicate it.
